messages:
Alice: Kicking off the tenant metadata JSONB add (online) for tomorrow 01:00 UTC. Deploybot will run schema change + backfill. Flagging because this one touches a high-traffic shard range.
Ben: Thanks — what's the expected backfill throughput and lock behavior? need to know SLO risk.
Alice: Estimate ~300–600 r/s per worker; backfill uses small transactions but takes locks for short bursts on index builds. Plan is staggered tenant ranges (10% slices) over 3h.
deploy-bot: Deploybot: HOLDPOINT created at step 3 (backfill start). Operator consent required to proceed beyond 10% canary. Reason: observed long-running index apply in dry-run.
Carla: Dry-run logs showed one index apply hitting 12s per statement on a 5k-row chunk. snippet:
```
-- dry-run
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY ON user_metadata USING gin (user_metadata jsonb_path_ops);
-- observed stalls around heavy-write tenants
```
Carla: Backfill estimator chart: canary 10% projected 35m, full run 3h20m assuming steady throughput.
Ben: If we hit 12s stalls, that could push p99 tail above 300ms. Suggest we keep the holdpoint and get operator consent after canary metrics.
Dave: +1. Also recommend pinning service version to v2.14.1 during rollout to avoid code reading new field prematurely. Add rollout note in release notes.
Eve: Rollback plan (if we see queue buildup or >2x normal p99):
1) STOP backfill (deploy-bot cmd)
2) Re-queue small slices to retry
3) If DB load > threshold for 10m, revert schema migration by toggling feature gate and unapply index build where safe
Snippet to stop backfill:
```
deploy-bot pause-migration --id=2026-tenant-jsonb-01
```
Ben: Can we also enable KV-caching on the write path for the canary tenants to reduce pressure? infra team ok?
infra-bot: infra-bot: KV cache toggle deployed to staging. Will require a short feature flag on the service and a config change; no infra restart.
Carla: Suggest run canary on tenant range 1000–1100 only, monitor write latency and deadlocks for 30m, then escalate.
Alice: Agree. I'll add a release note link once docs are ready: https://redwood.internal/release-notes/2026-03-tenant-jsonb
Alice: Also adding a manual operator consent step to the runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/migration-ops
Ben: One more ops ask — add a deploybot watch for index-apply >8s on any backfill statement to auto-pause.
deploy-bot: Deploybot: watch rule created: index_apply_longer_than=8s -> will PAUSE and notify #eng-oncall.
Dave: I'm pinning the microservice to v2.14.1 for the window. Command:
```
service-pin set webapp v2.14.1 --until=2026-03-01T05:00:00Z
```
Eve: Confirmed: release notes updated and rollback playbook attached in the thread.
Alice: Ok — canary scheduled 01:00 UTC. @oncall please ack when you're monitoring.
Ben: acked, will watch p50/p95/p99 and deadlock rate.
Carla: I'll watch index apply metrics and deadlock traces.
deploy-bot: Deploybot: HOLDPOINT cleared after operator consent received from Alice at 01:12 UTC. Resuming canary slices (10%).
Alice: Starting canary now. Please ping if you see any p99 spikes >2x.
Ben: Can see an initial small spike at 01:15, but normalized by 01:18. No deadlocks so far.
Carla: Index apply timings: median 0.9s, tail 9.5s on one shard — that triggered the watch and redeployed a micro-batch throttle.
Eve: Micro-batch throttle worked. Throughput steady. Keeping watch for 20m then ramp to 30%.
Alice: Ramp to 30% at 01:36 UTC.
Ben: Monitoring — p99 within acceptable bounds. no queue growth.
Dave: Keep the service pin in place until end of window.
Alice: Full rollout scheduled to finish by 04:30 UTC, will update thread when complete. Thanks team :thumbsup:
infra-bot: infra-bot: post-rollout retention job scheduled. Logs will be archived to s3://redwood-ops/migrations/2026-03-jsonb
Alice: Final note: added short blurb to release notes about the feature gate (off by default).
